claim: Fengjia Night Market in Taichung's Xitun District (around Feng Chia University) is one of Taiwan's largest night markets and a test-lab for new street-food trends.
quote: Fengjia Night Market is widely considered the largest and most innovative night market in Taiwan, located in the Xitun District surrounding Feng Chia University.

claim: Claims that Fengjia is the single largest market in Taiwan are unverified; it is confirmed as one of the largest, while Yizhong Street Night Market sits in central Taichung north of Taichung Park, walkable from the train station.
quote: claims that it is the largest in Taiwan, but this is difficult to say for sure... Yizhong Street: Central Taichung, north of Taichung Park; walkable from Taichung Train Station

claim: Chun Shui Tang of Taichung claims it invented bubble milk tea in March 1987 when staffer Lin Hsiu Hui poured tapioca into a tea drink; founder Liu Han-chieh had earlier experimented with cold cocktail-shaker teas.
quote: Chun Shui Tang... claims to have invented bubble milk tea in March 1987... Lin Hsiu Hui... poured tapioca into a tea drink on a whim

claim: The bubble-tea origin dispute pits Taichung's Chun Shui Tang (1988, Lin Hsiu Hui) against Tainan's Hanlin Tea Room (Tu Tsong-he), and a roughly decade-long lawsuit ended in 2019 with courts ruling bubble tea could not be patented or exclusively owned.
quote: Chun Shui Tang... Lin Hsiu Hui... poured tapioca balls into her tea... Hanlin Tea Room... Tu Tsong-he... courts reached a landmark decision in 2019 that determined bubble tea couldn't be patented or exclusively owned

claim: Suncakes (taiyang bing) are a flaky maltose-filled pastry originating in Taichung, first made by the Lin family in Shengang and later refined by Wei Qing-hai; they are sold in gift boxes as the city's signature souvenir.
quote: A suncake, or taiyang bing, is a popular Taiwanese dessert originally from the city of Taichung... The first suncakes were made by the Lin family... pastry maker Wei Qing-hai modified the cakes to their current form... usually sold in special gift boxes as souvenirs

claim: Yizhong Street Night Market caters to nearby students with budget snacks like Angel fried chicken fillet, half-moon flaky wrap pastries, hand-made stinky tofu and Fengren shaved ice, with NT$100-200 enough to sample several signature items.
quote: fatty chicken nuggets, half-moon-shaped snacks... spicy stinky tofu, Fengren Ice... Expect to spend NT$100-200 per person to sample 5-6 signature items

claim: Taichung has emerged as a specialty-coffee pilgrimage city, home to internationally ranked roasteries including Coffee Stopover (a World's Top 100 Cafe with in-house roasting) and Tomorrow Coffee, spanning industrial-chic to Japanese-minimalist concepts.
quote: Taichung... has recently emerged as a primary pilgrimage site for coffee enthusiasts... Coffee Stopover: Renowned for its in-house specialty roasting... recognized as one of the world's top 100 cafes in 2026... Tomorrow Coffee: A 2026 World Top 100 Cafe inductee

claim: Beyond markets, Taichung's daytime food scene includes traditional-market staples such as braised pork rice, radish cake, glutinous rice sausage and oyster congee, plus standalone spots like Shandong Dumpling & Noodle (est. 1996) for hand-rolled dumplings.
quote: Shandong Dumpling & Noodle, founded in 1996, sells authentic northern Chinese-style noodles and hand-rolled dumplings
